Q: How should loading, partial answers, abstention and committed outcomes appear in an AI interface?
A:
The interface should represent what the system actually knows: waiting, partial generated text, supported completion, insufficient evidence, failure and authoritative operation state. Streamed text is provisional content, not proof that a domain effect committed.

Preserve focus, readable status and a recoverable user action when a request fails. Feedback should attach to stable message or operation identities, not a transient screen position. Invalidate obsolete responses after account or conversation changes and avoid leaving private stale content visible.
Why: A user cancels while text is streaming. The interface can stop showing new text immediately but must separately check whether any requested backend effect was already accepted before describing the entire operation as cancelled.
Risk: An optimistic success label can contradict authoritative state.
Trade: Immediate feedback improves responsiveness when provisional and final states are clearly distinguished.
Try: Test every visible state, including a late old response after an identity switch.
